# Fixed PRIMARY literal runtime identity observation

This prospective successor observes the unchanged fixed268 literal paths on
EITHER exact known ubuntu24/Linux/X64 image20261025.353.1 or20261101.360.1.
The actual selected image is recorded, not substituted for original metadata.
Every other image/OS/architecture stops before source materialization; there
is no retry, fallback or automatic runner selection. The old single-image
queries and image-mismatch failures remain immutable and unqualified.

The manual workflow authenticates ROOT actor1981537/thread
01a18e7c-8c23-7fd2-8d55-b0486d938cd3, exact head/workflow SHA, first attempt,
and admission before fetching fixed hash/length-bound sources. It invokes the
unchanged portable resource/ownership guard directly with Python. No Node
wrapper, Go, Git, gcc, readelf, ldd, product or test is executed by the query.
Dormant earlier action/collector support files remain history, not inputs.

Each literal path is opened through nofollow parent descriptors and a nofollow
nonblocking leaf. Only regular files are hashed; the same descriptor is checked
before/after EOF and closed. Missing/unsafe/unreadable/changed observations are
explicit and never equal. A fatal deadline/read/close error retains all268
expected rows with remaining observations marked unobserved; it fails closed.
The original records are never replaced. Runtime libraries are code inputs,
not configuration. This does not discover a changed current dependency closure,
qualify execution, or authorize any construction or future runner.

Inherited bounds: bootstrap60s(+5s forced termination), one180s guard with10s
cleanup parameter per phase and .2s sampling, 24GiB sampled descendant RSS/free10GiB, 5min job,
1GiB common-workroot stage-boundary census/reservations, 1GiB cumulative input
read, complete2MiB joined console publication. Publication has20s(+5s forced
termination). The unchanged guard may use three10s cleanup phases plus a10s
join on an adverse path. Combined worst-case stage allowances can exceed the
5min outer; outer cancellation therefore cannot qualify cleanup/publication.
No positive receipt is inferred after cancellation. These are not instantaneous
storage/RSS guarantees. All new harness/tmp/log/receipt bytes are within the
common root. The host inputs remain read-only. Guard stdout/stderr/result are
published complete with sizes/hashes/base64 only after guard returns; publisher
checks stable regular single-link descriptors, EOF and close. Query failure,
cleanup intervention, missing receipt, output overbound or publication failure
cannot become PASS. No rerun or new build is selected by this source.

Focused source correction: the normal maintained guard schema omits pending
cleanup-signal observations; publication records that absence without inventing
an empty observed set. Recorded signals, guard errors, interventions and failed
statuses still refuse success. Every checked path-descriptor close failure is
terminal; sanitized operational errors precede cleanup errors in the retained
first-failure row. Python source under /etc (including sitecustomize.py) remains
code input, rather than configuration. No guard or resource predicate changed.

Prospective current-image scope: this fixed query records all268 immutable
expected rows, not a refreshed inventory. Exit0 means observations completed,
not that their identities equal the originals. ROOT must inspect every
equals_original/status plus original manifest binding and complete checked
publication before contemplating construction. Any mismatch, unavailable row,
partial output or failed guard/close is not qualification. This does not
authorize construction on the queried host or any future host. Use a fresh
metadata-only admission binding this branch head and expected_images equal to
the exact ordered two-image allowlist;
the dormant construction admission-template.json is not the query admission.

Bootstrap trust is unchanged: fixed hosted /usr/bin/python3.12 -I -B and its
platform standard library run before query-source materialization. They are
hosted-image trust inputs, not newly preauthenticated file bytes. Exact ROOT
actor/thread/head/workflow/first-attempt admission and the immutable allowlist
are checked before fetching hash/length-pinned query/guard helpers. The visit
records the original268 expected file identities versus actual/missing/unsafe
facts; it does not bless bootstrap drift or a complete current runtime closure.
No original interpreter/SDK/library identity is replaced, constructor predicate
relaxed, prior admission reused, or Go/tool/product executed. Constructor input
binding and any future execution need separate exact-source review/admission.

Failure-only bootstrap diagnosis adds constant IDs to the same assertions,
including nested census and fetch guards; their Boolean expressions and order
remain unchanged. The failure receipt includes class, one constant predicate,
and a bounded four-field image tuple. OS/architecture use only known literals
or missing_or_other; the public version rule is described below. Only the forbidden_ambient_flags failure includes
five presence booleans; it never includes their values. No arbitrary exception
text, traceback locals, cwd or private environment content is printed. Unknown
or nonassertion errors use non_assertion_or_unlabelled. Combined conditions
remain combined; a label identifies the original guard, not an unrecorded
subcause. This successor does not prove the prior ff9644 failure's predicate.
There is no added visit/probe/loop or automatic repeat; fresh review and ROOT
admission remain required. The fixed dispatch branch remains
diagnostic/primary-two-known-images-metadata-01.

The b83 failure identified `known_image` but its sanitization hid whether the
process version was absent or differed from the setup-log label. The failure
receipt now records presence and permits the existing public ImageVersion field
only when it is ASCII digits/dots, contains a digit and is at most 40 bytes.
Other values remain `missing_or_other`. This changes failure reporting only:
the two exact accepted image tuples and every authority/resource/input check
remain unchanged. It neither assumes a suffix nor admits an unlisted image.
